newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW-BRAZIL'S CPFL SEES SMOOTH H2.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BRAZIL'S CPFL SEES SMOOTH H2.

text.p: Earnings at Sao Paulo state power firm Cia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) will continue rising, but no major financial surprises are likely ahead of its slated November sale, a company official said.
"We will continue to improve in the second half but there should be no major fluctuations, no big surprises," CPFL's Financial Director Julio Colombi told Reuters in an interview.
"In this pre-privatization phase, everything should run normally," he said.
Colombi declined to project year-end earnings.
The company posted a 118 million-real net profit in 1996, he said.

In the first half, CPFL's non-adjusted net profit surged 92 percent to 77.1 million reais compared with 40.1 million reais in 1996's first six months. Revenues also were up in the period, totalling 933.7 million reais versus 906.9 million reais.

Colombi said the January-June results were helped by a rate hike in April, six percent market growth, cost-cutting efforts and gains from depreciation linked to a revaluation of company assets in June 1996.

Second-half financial results should continue to benefit from those factors, especially the efforts to rein in expenses. "The outlook is good now that we've gotten expenses under control," he said. "We should continue at the normal pace and generate a nice profit."
Second-half results also should be aided by the fact the company "has plenty of cash and no debts. We have absolute liquidity," he added.
Considered one of the most attractive of Brazil's power distributors, CPFL is expected to go on the auction block sometime between November 10 and November 30, Colombi said.
Company officials will be in New York starting August 25 and later travel to London and other European cities on a road show to promote the selloff, he said.
"Bid specifications should be published upon our return, sometime at the beginning of September," he added.
